newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: OCE denies liability in U.S antitrust suit.
newsitem.headline: OCE denies liability in U.S antitrust suit.

text.p: Dutch photocopier and printer maker Oce-van der Grinten NV (OCE) on Wednesday denied liability in a Florida lawsuit filed against various companies including Siemens Nixdorf Printing which Oce bought in September.

Oce said a class action had been filed by a number of independent service companies, alleging violations of Florida anti-trust laws beginning in 1993, against various Siemens units, AT & T Corp Global Information Solutions, and Oce Printing Systems USA (formerly Siemens Nixdorf Printing).

"The heart of the case is that several independent firms in printing machine maintainence allege the companies have acted in such a way as to make it impossible for them to carry out their business," an Oce spokesman said.

"Liabilities, if any, resulting from violations of such anti-trust laws prior to the acquisition by Oce of the HPP (high performance printing) division of Siemens Nixdorf were not assumed by Oce," a statement said.

The Oce spokesman said the Siemens AG units cited in the claim were: Siemens Nixdorf Printing Systems (now Oce Printing Systems), Siemens Credit Corp (Delaware), Siemens Nixdorf Information System Inc (Mass.) and Siemens Nixdorf Information System AG.
Oce's acquisition of Siemens Nixdorf Printing Systems was part of its global purchase of Siemens Nixdorf's high performance printing business announced in February.
"This particular deal (Siemens Nixdorf Printing Systems) was part of the worldwide one and was strictly an asset purchase. As such, we did not take on the liability," the spokesman said.
